definition: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) units and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) are types of RNN architectures designed to help capture information over extended sequences, useful in applications like time series prediction and natural language processing.
details: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) units and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) are types of RNN architectures designed to help capture information over extended sequences, useful in applications like time series prediction and natural language processing.

explainer.lead: LSTM and GRU are recurrent architectures built to retain information across long sequences. They matter because plain RNNs struggle to carry context over extended spans.

tiers.eli5: Think of a reader who keeps a running notebook of what matters so far, instead of forgetting the start of the story by the end.
tiers.practitioner: Used for time series prediction and NLP where sequence order matters; a pitfall is that they process steps sequentially, which limits parallel training.
tiers.paperLevel: Gated recurrent units that control information flow through learned gates to mitigate vanishing gradients; limits include sequential computation and finite memory.

explainer.example: An LSTM forecasts next-hour energy demand from a series of past readings, retaining patterns across many timesteps.
